headline: Paraguay President Santiago Peña Resigns and Is Impeached After Bank Collapse
summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigned and was impeached by lawmakers following the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government, which left three million customers unable to access accounts.
why: Political instability and systemic banking crises in emerging markets can trigger sharp sovereign risk repricing, currency depreciation, and disruptions in local credit markets.

impacts.name: Paraguay
impacts.why: The presidential resignation and bank collapse directly destabilize the country's political and financial governance.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The sudden collapse of the digital bank and the impeachment of the president create extreme domestic political uncertainty and systemic risk for the financial sector.
